questions.q: 2-Methylpropene reacts with HBr in the absence of peroxide. The product is:
questions.explain: H⁺ adds to the CH₂ end to give the tertiary carbocation, which Br⁻ captures. The other orientation would need a primary carbocation, so 1-bromo-2-methylpropane does not form.

questions.q: The correct order of reactivity of hydrogen halides towards addition to an alkene is:
questions.explain: The H–X bond gets weaker down the group, so H⁺ is transferred more easily: HI > HBr > HCl, much greater than HF.

questions.q: Buta-1,3-diene reacts with one equivalent of HBr at low temperature. The major product, and the reason, is:
options: 3-Bromobut-1-ene, because it has the lower activation energy and forms faster
questions.explain: At low temperature the steps are not reversible, so the kinetic 1,2-adduct (lower Ea) dominates. 1-Bromobut-2-ene is the more stable thermodynamic product that wins at higher temperature.

questions.q: Isopropenylcyclobutane reacts with HBr. Allowing for every rearrangement of the carbocation, the major product is:
questions.explain: The tertiary cation first expands the strained four-membered ring to a five-membered one, then a methyl shift creates a tertiary cation, which Br⁻ captures. Stopping after ring expansion gives the 2,2-dimethyl distractor.
